advances: Ordinary planar caps in the Hausdorff topology. Perturbations need not be strictly convex; no shape reduction for arbitrary bodies.

proof:
Cycle the coordinates to take $i=1$, with positive vertical endpoint $P=(0,h)$. Let $L_\varepsilon=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{P_\varepsilon\})$ with $P_\varepsilon=P+(0,\varepsilon)$. The added region localizes at $P$: if along $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ there were points $x_\varepsilon\in L_\varepsilon\setminus K$ outside a fixed neighborhood of $P$, take a subsequence converging to $x$ and unit strict separating normals converging to $n$. The hull inclusion $L_\varepsilon\subseteq K+\varepsilon B_2$ gives $x\in K$. For each separating normal $n_\varepsilon$, $n_\varepsilon\cdot x_\varepsilon>h_K(n_\varepsilon)$ forces $n_\varepsilon\cdot P_\varepsilon>h_K(n_\varepsilon)$ by convexity of the hull. Thus $n\cdot P=n\cdot x=h_K(n)$. Strict convexity makes the support face a singleton, contradicting $x$ outside the neighborhood.

Choose the neighborhood in $y>0,\ x+y>0$ and away from a fixed interior ball about $0$. The fill lies in signatures $\{1,2\}$ on $x>0$ and $\{2\}$ on $x<0$, with respective positive areas $D_{12},D_2$. Positivity follows because a small exterior ball at $P_\varepsilon$ meets the cone from that point to the interior ball on both sides of $x=0$ in positive-area sets. The total $D=D_{12}+D_2$ tends to zero by the outer parallel set inclusion. Choose $R$ on the boundary of $K$ on the positive diagonal ray. A support $\ell$ there uniquely exposes $R$ by strict convexity. Choose a fixed shallow positive-depth cap $\ell\ge\ell(R)-t_0$ that lies in the open positive quadrant and is separated from $P$. This is possible because the caps shrink to $R$ as their depth decreases, and $\ell(P)<\ell(R)$. By fill locality, for small $\varepsilon$ this fixed halfspace has the same trace on $L_\varepsilon$ as on $K$. By continuity of parallel cap areas it can be replaced by a shallower halfspace of trace area exactly $D$. Cutting it off removes only signature $\{1,2\}$, avoids the source lines, and leaves the origin interior. Its depth tends to zero since every fixed positive-depth cap has positive area. Hence its removed piece shrinks to $R$ and the modified bodies converge to $K$ in Hausdorff distance.

The two other chords are unchanged by the localization. Since $P_\varepsilon$ is on $x=0$, every point of $L_\varepsilon$ on that line is a convex combination of $P_\varepsilon$ with an old point on the same line, or is $P_\varepsilon$ itself. Thus the upper endpoint moves exactly $\varepsilon$ and the lower endpoint stays fixed. The changes in cap areas are $(-D_2,0,0)$ and in coarea chords $(\varepsilon,0,0)$, at constant total area. The normalized inverse weight and sorted profile conclusions follow from the same elementary monotonicities: the selected inverse chord decreases and the others stay fixed before normalization, and every order statistic of the cap areas is coordinatewise nondecreasing. Cycling the normals scales all coareas by the common area Jacobian and preserves normalized weights. The new cut may leave a line segment, so the local minimum conclusion uses the full feasible class.

statement: Use the three normals $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$ through the interior mark $0$. For a planar convex body $K$, let $q_i$ be the cap areas, $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap v_i^\perp)/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $\lambda_i=(1/\sigma_i)/\sum_j(1/\sigma_j)$. Assume $K$ is compact and strictly convex. For every selected index $i$, there are convex bodies converging to $K$ in Hausdorff distance, containing $0$ in their interiors, preserving total area and the other two cap areas and coarea chord lengths, strictly decreasing $q_i$ and increasing $\sigma_i$. Thus $\lambda_i$ strictly decreases while any initially satisfied bounds $q_j\le c_j|K|$ and $q_{\min}+q_{\mathrm{mid}}+q_{\max}/4\le |K|$ remain satisfied. By choosing an initially minimal $\lambda_i$, the minimum of the three weights also strictly decreases. In particular $K$ is not a local minimum of either specified objective in the full feasible convex-body class.
title: A strictly convex planar body cannot locally minimize a selected inverse chord weight
